The black-and-yellow striped bollards, granite-edged paving, and modernist apartment blocks with roller shutters point strongly to Portugal. The density of mid-rise towers, the mixed deciduous trees and the bright winter sun suggest the Porto area, possibly the Boavista or Matosinhos side of the city.

The white Renault Clio, the French no-entry sign and the yellow curb paint point clearly to France. The van shows a phone number beginning 05 62, which is the area code for Hautes-Pyrénées and Gers in the southwest. The half-timbered house, slate roofs, the red and white brick decoration on the corner and the stone walls fit a Bigorre town, most likely Tarbes.

>>> {"country":"France","place":"Tarbes, Hautes-Pyrénées","lat":43.2328,"lng":0.0781}

The plain postwar stone station building, with a long canopy and parked scooters on platform 1, fits a mid-size station on the Bologna–Ancona route. Rimini is my best guess, though Pesaro or Bologna Centrale are real possibilities.

>>> {"country":"Italy","place":"Rimini","lat":44.0640,"lng":12.5735}

The likeliest spot is a corridor like Washington Boulevard or the road toward Portmore, or Hellshire in St. Catherine.

>>> {"country":"Jamaica","place":"Portmore, St. Catherine","lat":17.9600,"lng":-76.8700}

>>> {"country":"Thailand","place":"Khao San Road, Bangkok","lat":13.7589,"lng":100.4974}

Left-hand traffic, a red three-wheeler tuk-tuk, Sinhala text on the billboard and a Texstretch advertisement point firmly to Sri Lanka. The busy multi-lane urban road with a median fence, a mushroom-shaped concrete water tower and a mosque minaret suggest coastal Colombo. My best guess is the Galle Road corridor around Dehiwala.

>>> {"country":"Sri Lanka","place":"Dehiwala, Colombo","lat":6.8510,"lng":79.8655}

The billboard text is in Hungarian ("Csatlakozz..."), and the blue lane-direction sign follows the European style, so this is Hungary. The old ochre multi-storey building with many chimneys, the wide urban arterial with tram-era paving, and the hilly backdrop suggest the Buda side of Budapest. It looks like a main road leading out toward the Buda hills, possibly the Budaörsi út or Hegyalja út area in District XI.

>>> {"country":"Hungary","place":"Budapest, District XI","lat":47.4800,"lng":19.0250}

The flat terrain, lush green trees, bright sunny sky and the half-finished concrete-block buildings fit the humid Black Sea lowlands of Adjara. Of those, the outskirts of Batumi are the most likely spot.

>>> {"country":"Georgia","place":"Batumi, Adjara","lat":41.6200,"lng":41.6100}

Together they place this at the Wien Mitte transport hub in Vienna's 3rd district, Landstraße. Bikes parked in large numbers, street lamps hung on wires across the road, and granite slab sidewalks with cobblestone edging strips are classic Copenhagen streetscape features. The red-brick building and the big mid-century stone office blocks with flags suggest central Copenhagen, near the inner ring by Vesterbro and the Lakes.

>>> {"country":"Denmark","place":"Copenhagen","lat":55.6788,"lng":12.5620}

The leafy, villa-lined streets with mature trees suggest a wealthier residential area in North Holland, such as Haarlem, Heemstede or Bloemendaal. I'm going with Haarlem.

>>> {"country":"Netherlands","place":"Haarlem","lat":52.3720,"lng":4.6420}

Wide avenues with cobbled medians, yellow kerbs and an overcast, Mediterranean-looking setting all fit central Santiago. The Gothic-style church in cream and yellow, plus the tall structures nearby, point to the older districts just south of downtown, possibly around Avenida Matta.

>>> {"country":"Chile","place":"Santiago, Santiago Centro","lat":-33.457,"lng":-70.648}

>>> {"country":"Portugal","place":"Rua Augusta, Baixa, Lisbon","lat":38.7115,"lng":-9.1376}

The parking area for motorhomes (Sunlight and other caravans) sits beside a flat, calm lagoon with small low islands. That fits the Venetian Lagoon well, most likely the Fusina terminal and camper parking area near Venice.

>>> {"country":"Italy","place":"Fusina, Venice","lat":45.4185,"lng":12.2565}

The French road markings, painted bike lanes and green wheelie bins fit as well. This mix of bourgeois brick townhouses on a long straight street is typical of Amiens, along the 19th-century streets south of the centre.

>>> {"country":"France","place":"Amiens","lat":49.8880,"lng":2.2920}

Several right-hand-drive Japanese cars, including the white minivan, suggest Siberia, where imported Japanese used cars are common. The flat, wide boulevard with an overpass and a birch-poplar greenbelt fits a large city like Novosibirsk.

>>> {"country":"Russia","place":"Novosibirsk","lat":55.0650,"lng":82.9200}

>>> {"country":"Philippines","place":"Intramuros, Manila","lat":14.5903,"lng":120.9748}

text:
A McLouis motorhome on a Fiat Ducato base is a brand sold mostly in France and Italy, and the older Mercedes A-Class beside it fits a European setting. The Aleppo/stone pines, Italian cypresses, pale limestone gravel and strong dry sunlight all point to a Mediterranean inland area, most likely Provence. I'm placing it in the Vaucluse/Bouches-du-Rhône area.

With no signs or other cultural clues, this is a low-confidence guess, but the hilly park terrain resembles Zagreb's Medvednica foothills or Maksimir area, so I'll place it near Zagreb, Croatia.

Together with the green directional sign, this points to an Irish national primary road or dual carriageway. The overcast sky, lush grass verges, conifer plantations and post-and-wire fencing fit the Irish midlands, though nothing in the photo pins down which road, so the exact spot is a guess.

The mix of rubber and coffee strongly suggests Vietnam's Central Highlands, around Đắk Lắk or Gia Lai, though Brazil or West Africa can't be ruled out.

The low-rise, older-looking commercial strip with small hardware and household-goods shops suggests one of the northern emirates rather than Dubai or Abu Dhabi. The smiley-face green traffic light and the overall feel of the street lean towards Ajman, though that part is less certain.

>>> {"country":"United Arab Emirates","place":"Ajman","lat":25.4000,"lng":55.4700}

PART 1: A Hymer Eriba camper is parked on a seafront promenade. A low concrete sea wall sits behind it, with a flat, low far shore across a wide estuary or bay. The paving and kerbs look British or Irish, and the van is a right-hand-drive Fiat Ducato. The scene resembles Salthill Promenade in Galway or Dundalk, but the flat low far shore fits the Shannon estuary at Limerick or Kilrush, or Sligo. I'm committing to Salthill-ish Galway Bay, though the far shore there is the Burren hills, not flat. The flat shoreline better matches Clontarf in Dublin Bay or Dundalk Bay, so I'll go with Dundalk Bay at Blackrock.

>>> {"country":"Portugal","place":"Viseu district","lat":40.7,"lng":-7.9}

The European cars, Italian-style road signs and the Italian text on the yellow car also fit. The steep cliff face is on the eastern side of the mountain, so the photo was most likely taken from a parking lot at the eastern foot, perhaps near the Baldasserona area. That spot is my lower-confidence inference.
